issues.t: Automatic transmission failure on the RX300
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring revs between gears, late or harsh engagement into drive or reverse, or a flashing O/D light.
issues.why: The first-generation automatic is known for wearing out internally, with owners reporting full failures. Old, broken-down fluid and towing add heat and speed up the wear.
issues.next: Have the fluid level and condition checked and the transmission scanned at the first sign of slipping. Avoid towing and heavy loads until it is looked at, since a slipping unit tends to get worse fast.

issues.t: Engine oil sludge (oil gelling)
issues.sym: Oil pressure light flickering, rising oil use, blue smoke, or ticking from the top of the engine.
issues.why: Oil in this engine could thicken into sludge and block oil passages, especially with long gaps between oil changes. Toyota and Lexus set up a special policy for sludge damage, and the RX300 was part of a later class settlement.
issues.next: Change the oil on a short schedule with quality oil. If the oil pressure light comes on, stop driving and have the engine inspected before running it again.

issues.t: Floor carpet cover can hold the gas pedal down (recall)
issues.sym: The accelerator feels like it is sticking partly pressed, or the vehicle does not slow down as expected when you lift off the pedal.
issues.why: A carpet cover that was not secured properly could lean against the accelerator pedal arm and keep it from returning.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the fix done. Remove any loose or extra floor mats on the driver side right away.

issues.t: Radiator can crack and leak coolant
issues.sym: Coolant drips or crust near the radiator, a low coolant level, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: On some early second-generation RX models the radiator could crack where the tubes meet the tank. Lexus ran a service campaign and extra coverage to replace it.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level and ask a Lexus dealer whether the campaign was done on your VIN. Do not keep driving if the engine runs hot.

issues.t: Dashboard cracks, turns shiny or gets sticky
issues.sym: Cracks across the dash top, a tacky or melted surface, or glare reflecting into the windshield.
issues.why: Heat and humidity break down the dashboard material over time. Lexus extended coverage on affected vehicles under a warranty enhancement, though that window has mostly closed.
issues.next: Use a dash cover if glare makes it hard to see. Ask a Lexus dealer whether any coverage still applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Engine oil cooler hose can burst
issues.sym: A sudden oil leak at the front of the engine, oil spray or smoke, a burning oil smell, or the oil warning light.
issues.why: A rubber section of the oil cooler line can crack and dump oil quickly. Lexus replaced it with an all-metal line under an extended warranty program.
issues.next: Have the line inspected and swapped for the metal version if it was never done. If the oil light comes on, pull over and shut the engine off.

issues.t: VVT-i oil supply hose can rupture (campaign)
issues.sym: Heavy oil leak from the top or side of the engine, low oil warning, or oil burning on hot parts.
issues.why: A rubber hose feeding oil to the variable valve timing system can split under pressure. Lexus replaced it with an all-metal line under a service campaign.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the campaign and get it done if it is open. Stop driving immediately if the oil light comes on.

issues.t: Floor mat can trap the gas pedal (recall)
issues.sym: The accelerator sticks down or the vehicle keeps speeding up after you lift off the pedal.
issues.why: An unsecured or wrong floor mat can catch the accelerator pedal and hold it open.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Use only the correct, clipped-in driver mat and never stack mats.

issues.t: ABS and stability control may not control one wheel properly (recall)
issues.sym: Longer stopping distances during hard braking or when stability control steps in.
issues.why: A calibration error in a hydraulic control valve could keep the right front wheel from being controlled correctly when ABS or VSC is working.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it fixed before relying on the vehicle in slippery conditions.

issues.t: Brake actuator fault turns off ABS and stability control (recall)
issues.sym: ABS, VSC or traction control warning lights come on, and those systems stop working.
issues.why: An electrical part in the brake actuator could act up and set fault codes. Lexus fixes it with a software update.
issues.next: Normal brakes still work, but drive gently in rain or snow and get the recall done soon.

issues.t: Fuel delivery pipe can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell around the vehicle or under the hood, or wetness near the engine.
issues.why: A fuel pipe in the engine bay could leak fuel, which is a fire risk near hot parts.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park it and have it towed. Check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: ABS actuator seal problem (recall)
issues.sym: Brake or stability warnings, or braking that feels uneven when ABS or traction control kicks in.
issues.why: A damaged O-ring in the ABS actuator could let brake pressure act incorrectly during ABS, traction or stability control use.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it repaired promptly.

issues.t: Air bags may not deploy correctly (recalls)
issues.sym: Often no warning, though an air bag light may come on.
issues.why: On some 2016 models, crash sensors could fail and the driver knee air bag inflator could leak gas because of a poor weld.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls and get them done as soon as possible.

issues.t: "Braking Power Low" warning at startup
issues.sym: A Braking Power Low message on startup or while driving, sometimes with a no-start.
issues.why: Lexus issued a bulletin for this warning on some RX 350s. It is tied to the brake booster system.
issues.next: Do not ignore it. Have a Lexus dealer check for the bulletin and the brake booster pump, and make sure the brakes work normally before driving.

issues.t: Brake booster vacuum pump can fail (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly feels hard and the vehicle takes more effort and distance to stop.
issues.why: A rotor inside the vacuum pump for the brake booster could be machined wrong and fail, cutting brake assist.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If the pedal goes hard, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Droning noise at light throttle
issues.sym: A low hum or drone from under the car when pulling away or cruising lightly, sometimes with a buzz in the center console.
issues.why: Lexus issued bulletins for exhaust droning on many RX 350s. The fix adds parts to the exhaust, and some owners still notice it afterward.
issues.next: It is a comfort issue, not a safety one. Ask a Lexus dealer to check for the exhaust droning bulletins.

issues.t: Hesitation or jerky shifts at low speed
issues.sym: A pause when pulling away or passing, or a jerk right after a gear change at low speed.
issues.why: Lexus released bulletins and software updates for drivability complaints on this generation of the RX 350.
issues.next: Have a Lexus dealer check for updated transmission and engine software.

issues.t: AWD rear coupling noise
issues.sym: A grinding, whine or clunk from the rear, or the AWD system acting strangely.
issues.why: The rear coupling on the Dynamic Torque Control AWD system can make noise or misbehave. Lexus issued a bulletin for it.
issues.next: Have a Lexus dealer inspect the rear differential coupling and check for the bulletin.

issues.t: Chirping from the high-pressure fuel pump
issues.sym: A chirp or tick from the engine at idle.
issues.why: The high-pressure fuel pump can make this noise on some RX 350s. Lexus issued a bulletin for it.
issues.next: It is usually harmless, but have it checked if it gets louder or the engine runs rough.

issues.t: In-tank fuel pump can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, warning lights, loss of power, or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump inside the tank could stop working, which can stall the engine at speed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for these recalls and get them done. If the engine stumbles or stalls, get it to a dealer before driving far.

issues.t: Passenger seat sensor can switch off the air bag (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger air bag OFF light stays on with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: The occupant sensor in the front passenger seat could misread who is sitting there and turn the air bag off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and get it fixed soon.

issues.t: Driver air bag may be disabled (recall)
issues.sym: The air bag warning light comes on, or steering wheel buttons stop working.
issues.why: A bad weld in the steering column spiral cable could separate and cut power to the driver air bag.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it repaired promptly.

issues.t: Backup camera picture can fail (recall)
issues.sym: The rearview camera image is blank, frozen or distorted when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: Lexus recalled many non-hybrid RX models because a defect in the rear camera could stop it from showing an image.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Until it is fixed, use your mirrors and look behind you when backing up.
src: Lexus backup camera recall, March 2026 (2023-2026 non-hybrid RX)

issues.t: Front steering knuckle may be weak (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning before it breaks. After hitting a pothole or curb, steering could feel off or the wheel could shift.
issues.why: One batch of forged aluminum front knuckles skipped a heat-treatment step at the supplier, leaving them weaker than designed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall right away and follow the dealer instructions. Avoid potholes and curbs until it is inspected.
